sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Ultra-HD 4K Minimally Invasive Rigid Endoscopes

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–United States Income Tax Convention (1994, as amended)
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT); Article L561-45 et seq. (UBO filing); Decree No. 2019-1179 of 14 November 2019; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as transposed by Ordinance No. 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Ultimate Beneficial Owner(s) (e.g., foreign corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Companies Registrar of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Existence Certificate of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register or Companies House of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or Government-issued ID of each natural person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National identification authority of country of nationality/residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if country is not a Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Subscribed and paid-up capital evidence or bank reference letter for non-resident investors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (for bank attestations)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons per Article L561-10 CMF; systematic screening against UN Security Council consolidated list, EU autonomous sanctions list, French Treasury asset-freeze list, and OFAC SDN list; screening must be documented and retained per Article L561-12-1 CMF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) / Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by INPI
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be written in Latin script; non-Latin alphabets must be transliterated into Latin/French spelling. The name must comply with French public policy, must not mislead the public, and must be available in the RNE/INPI database. French language laws require a French-language version for local commercial communication, but registration may use a foreign name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal by the INPI/RNE, the applicant may file a written administrative review request with INPI within two months of notification. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may contest the decision before the Civil Court (Tribunal judiciaire) or Commercial Court (Tribunal de commerce), as appropriate, within three months, seeking annulment of the registry decision and damages if the refusal is arbitrary.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible for a SAS manufacturing regulated medical devices; a physical registered office and operational premises in France are required to satisfy commercial substance and ANSM/ANSP licensing requirements. A virtual office may be used only for ancillary administrative functions after the physical establishment is operational and registered.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — an unannounced on-site inspection by ANSM (Agence nationale de sécurité sanitaire des aliments, de l'environnement et du travail) or the Ministry of Health is probable within the first 12 months of operation (risk exceeding 80%).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of Articles of Association (Statuts) and pre-incorporation legal advisory
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark (hourly rates of Paris-based corporate counsel)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation notice in a legal gazette (Journal d'annonces légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by prefectural order

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of incorporation dossier through Guichet Unique / RNE (including RNE fees)
Domiciliation of registered office (via approved domiciliation company)
Notarization and apostille/legalization of foreign UBO documents (per bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention of 5 October 1961; flat consular fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening including OFAC/UN/EU databases (per entity)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS), and Decree No. 2023-1 on the Guichet Unique
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) via the Guichet Unique (one-stop shop)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and Registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital required; if capital is set, at least 50% must be paid up at incorporation, remainder within 5 years. Funds must be deposited in a bank account or with a notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders hereby subscribe to the share capital of the company as set forth in the Articles of Association, and that the registered office is established at [address]. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as President, [Name] as General Manager, and [Name] as Treasurer, each to hold until replaced. The President is authorized to execute all documents necessary for the incorporation and registration of the company, including the filing with the Guichet Unique and the publication of the legal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Sign Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts in French, including company name, registered office, share capital, share distribution, and management structure. All shareholders must sign. If real estate is contributed, notarization is mandatory.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is required, engage a notary to authenticate the document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Share Capital in Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in France, deposit the share capital, and obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage de fonds).
required_dossiers: Proof of address of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses, use a notary to hold the funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Legal Notice in a Legal Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcement journal (JAL) approved by the prefecture
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice of incorporation in a legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) containing company name, registered office, capital, and management. Obtain a proof of publication (attestation de parution).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is rejected, correct the notice and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online form on the Guichet Unique, upload the required documents, pay the filing fee, and submit. The system transmits to the RCS and other authorities.
required_dossiers: Proof of publication of legal notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the request for additional information within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, the company is registered in the RCS and receives an extract (extrait Kbis) and SIRET number. This is the official proof of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, contact the Greffe for status.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé (ANSM) and notified body under EU MDR
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: CE Marking (Conformité Européenne) under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 for Medical Devices

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique (via DREAL - Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Déclaration) for low-risk manufacturing; full EIA required if significant emissions or chemical substances are used
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with French Environmental Code (Code de l'environnement) for wastewater (COD, BOD, pH limits), VOC emissions thresholds per ICPE, and waste handling per REACH and CLP regulations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire department (SDIS), structural load inspection by a certified engineer, and workplace clearance from the labor inspectorate (Inspection du travail) for occupational health and safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); professional portal: impots.gouv.fr; business formalities single window: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique); customs authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) with DELTA H1 export clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Incorporate the SAS via the Guichet Unique (single electronic window) by filing French articles of association (statuts), appointing a president, declaring the registered office in France and opening a French corporate bank account; the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) issues the K-bis extract with SIREN/SIRET and NAF code 3250B; the DGFiP automatically attributes the French intra-community VAT number (FR + 11-digit SIREN-based key), reflected on the taxpayer identification notice and in the VIES registry; for immediate import/export operations the SAS must also obtain an EORI number from the DGDDI. A foreign entity without a French establishment that makes direct taxable supplies into France must file a VAT identification request with the competent SIE under Article 289 A CGI and appoint a fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) when not established in the EU; the medical device activity must additionally be notified to ANSM under Article L.5211-3-2 of the French Public Health Code for CE-marked surgical endoscopy equipment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the SAS is by default subject to French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés 'IS') at the standard rate of 25% on its French-attribute profits, applying the French territoriality principle whereby foreign permanent establishment profits are generally exempt under Article 209-I CGI; no general pass-through regime applies to the SAS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not apply a US-style check-the-box regime. Available permanent elections include: (i) the Article 239 bis AB CGI option for a newly created SAS to be taxed as a transparent partnership under personal income tax for up to five fiscal years; (ii) the Article 223 A CGI election by a French parent SAS for tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) of qualifying French subsidiaries; (iii) the Article 209 A CGI election for worldwide taxation for five years (instead of territoriality); (iv) the VAT franchise option for small businesses. Hybrid mismatch arrangements are restricted: ATAD/ATAD 2 rules transposed in Articles 209 and 212 bis CGI disallow deductions for hybrid financial instruments, hybrid entities and double-dip arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, 'TVA')
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Goods: EUR 91,000 annual taxable turnover for the franchise en base de TVA, with a EUR 101,000 upper limit not to be exceeded; services: EUR 40,000 (upper limit EUR 44,000). A purely exporting medical-device manufacturer should register voluntarily at inception to recover input VAT on components, R&D and overheads; registration is mandatory from the day the threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured e-invoicing and e-reporting under the 2023 Réforme de la facturation électronique: from 1 September 2026 all VAT-registered businesses must receive electronic invoices, and large/mid-sized entities must issue them through a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenariale (PDP) or the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) using Factur-X / UBL / CII formats via API; SMEs follow on 1 September 2027. Transaction and payment data (e-reporting) is transmitted to the DGFiP in near real-time, complemented by the annual FEC file. For exports, fiscal clearance is electronic through the DELTA H1 (ECS) declaration with a Movement Reference Number (MRN); France does not apply physical fiscal stamping or QR-code clearance, but the DGDDI runs real-time risk scoring with the crédit d'enlèvement procedure for goods leaving French customs territory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of surgical laparoscopy towers and rigid endoscopes to non-EU destinations are exempt with credit (0% VAT) under Article 262-I-1° CGI provided title and possession are transferred to the non-EU purchaser and the goods physically leave EU customs territory unchanged; intra-EU dispatches are exempt under Article 262 ter CGI where the customer's intra-community VAT number is declared and the recapitulative statement is filed under Article 289 bis CGI; direct services tied to offshore installation, repair or technical support of medical devices supplied to a non-EU B2B recipient may be zero-rated under Article 259 A CGI.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation DAU via DELTA H1 ECS, bearing the MRN)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank confirmation of foreign-currency repatriation from the non-EU purchaser)
Commercial Invoice, Packing List and, if applicable, Certificate of Origin / EUR.1 movement certificate
Intra-community sales list / recapitulative statement (Article 289 bis CGI) for EU dispatches
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export proof documentation must be retained for at least 6 years for tax purposes (Article L102 B Livre des procédures fiscales) and for the applicable customs period (Article 65 Code des douanes). Where the 0% rate is claimed on missing, false or manipulated documentation, the DGFiP re-invoices VAT at 20% and applies monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% (Article 1727 CGI); a deliberate misstatement triggers the 40% bad-faith penalty (Article 1729 CGI), or 80% for manœuvres frauduleuses. Criminal customs sanctions (Code des douanes, Articles 414 et seq.) include confiscation of goods, fines of up to twice the goods' value, and imprisonment up to 10 years for organized fraud; joint and several liability applies under Article 283-2 CGI for circular MTIC-type fraud, and flagrant cases are referred to the Commission des Infractions Fiscales for criminal tax prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as the national central bank, exercising foreign-exchange administration jointly with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) under the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique. Monetary policy for the eurozone is delegated to the European Central Bank (ECB). The operative legal source is the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for both current-account and capital-account operations. France has accepted Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement and applies the EU free movement of capital regime under TFEU Articles 63-66 and Directive 88/361/EEC. The EUR is freely convertible; no prior administrative authorization applies to inbound or outbound payments, dividend and profit remittance, repayment of shareholder advances, or liquidation distributions. Residual compliance gates are: (1) EU/UN financial sanctions and asset-freeze orders; (2) French AML obligations under CMF Article L561-1 et seq.; (3) Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declarations for cross-border transactions reaching EUR 750,000 or more per transaction; and (4) the EUR 10,000 cash-movement declaration under CMF Article L152-1 and EU Regulation 2018/1672. Profit remittance from the French SAS to an EU parent is exempt from withholding tax under EU Directive 2011/96/EU where the parent holds at least 10% for 24 months; dividends to non-EU residents suffer a 25% French withholding rate, subject to treaty reduction. No practical hurdle exists for a manufacturing entity with legitimate medical-device operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France eliminated mandatory surrender of export proceeds in 1989 as part of the liberalization of exchange controls. There is no statutory conversion timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. The exporter may retain USD, CNY, or JPY balances in a French or EEA authorized credit institution; the annual statutory accounts must be kept in EUR and foreign-currency balances are revalued at the ECB reference rate at year-end. Only statistical reporting to the Banque de France may apply when the monthly or per-transaction cross-border payment threshold is exceeded.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Primary operational account (compte de dépôt) plus dedicated share-capital escrow account (compte séquestre) for the initial contribution
Operational account (compte courant) with integrated trade-finance desk for SWIFT LC issuance and documentary collections

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. (via a Caisse Régionale and LCL)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account and cash-management hub with access to regional business centers

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Natixis S.A. / Groupe BPCE (Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Épargne network)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account with dedicated global markets and FX hedging line

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Mutuel / CIC (Crédit Industriel et Commercial S.A.)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account and corporate FX/Treasury management account for USD-heavy settlement flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-Medium as the sole bank, acceptable only as a complementary disbursement channel. EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Treezor, Bunq, Revolut Business, and Wise Business can operate in France under the EMI passport regime of CMF Article L525-1 et seq. and may open a professional account remotely for a French SAS. However, EMIs are legally and practically unsuitable as the primary treasury bank for this issuer because: (1) they cannot issue or confirm documentary credits under ICC UCP 600 since they lack banking-partner credit-intermediation powers; (2) they act through bank sponsors, inserting an intermediation layer and settlement counterparty into the SWIFT MT103 chain; (3) electronic money floats must be safeguarded, not held freely, making working-capital sweeps less efficient; (4) they generally do not provide the Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting service, leaving the statutory declaration burden on the client; (5) foreign-currency accounts and natural FX positions are limited. Recommended structure: BNP Paribas or Société Générale as the relationship bank for LC and wires; a single EMI (e.g., Qonto) for expense cards and low-value disbursements capped at EUR 10,000 per transaction, swept daily to the operational account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default expectation but can be replaced by ANSSI-certified video identification (PVID) for the beneficial owner and signatories. Under CMF Article R561-5-2, identity may be verified by a certified electronic identification means; in practice, Tier-1 French banks require at least one physical onboarding interview for a non-resident shareholder or the chairman of the SAS at the Paris branch of the bank. Remote opening is permissible where the director's identity has been verified by an ANSSI-approved French digital identity solution, or where a French notaire or embassy apostilles and certifies the passport copy. The SAS president may alternatively grant a notarized power of attorney (POA) to a resident French attorney with a signature mandate. Account activation generally takes 15-30 business days after the physical interview and full document upload; documentary letter-of-credit facilities are typically activated only after three months of transactional history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) tax-resident in a non-CRS or high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certified copy of passport with apostille; (2) proof of address not older than 3 months; (3) tax-residency certificate from the home tax administration under the CRS/MCAA exchange framework; (4) professional curriculum vitae and board minute appointing the director; (5) reference letter from an existing prime banking relationship; (6) PEP declaration, with enhanced due-diligence file if PEPS.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ownership chain exceeding two intermediate holding layers or opaque trust structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Signed group organizational chart; (2) extract of the French Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) filed at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; (3) certified constitutional documents of each intermediate holding entity; (4) French counsel legal opinion identifying the UBO under CMF Article L561-2-3; (5) audited financial statements of the direct shareholder evidencing economic substance and commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial share-capital injection wired by a related party not pre-identified in the bank mandate
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Share subscription deed and articles of association; (2) SWIFT MT103 of the inbound transfer with remittance reference Apport en capital - souscription SAS; (3) 12-month bank statements of the remitter; (4) valuation report of the Commissaire aux Comptes if in-kind contribution; (5) signed statement of source of funds confirming the legitimate origin of the capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export of surgical laparoscopy towers to an end-destination flagged by EU sanctions or dual-use screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) CE certificate for the class IIa/IIb medical device under EU Regulation 2017/745 issued by an ANSM-notified body; (2) French customs export license or exemption letter from the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects; (3) end-user certificate from the purchasing hospital or authorized distributor; (4) ERP-generated compliance file matching purchase order, pro-forma invoice, LC, bill of lading, and customs entry; (5) internal sanctions-screening log evidencing checks against the EU and UN consolidated lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected turnover inconsistent with the medical-device manufacturing profile or with procurement pipelines
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Signed EU distribution agreement; (2) hospital tenders and confirmed purchase orders in the pipeline; (3) supplier framework agreements for 4K CMOS sensors, rigid endoscope optics, and LED light sources; (4) business plan benchmarked to ISIC 3250 industry margins; (5) historical audited financials of the controlling shareholder guaranteeing the projection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder transfers the initial subscription and any subsequent equity contributions via SWIFT MT103 or, for EEA-origin EUR, via SEPA Credit Transfer. The payment must identify the beneficiary as FR_SAS with the remittance reference Souscription au capital social - FR_SAS, and include the ISO 20022 purpose code for equity (e.g., Equi). All funds must be blocked on a dedicated share-capital escrow account (compte séquestre) held with a French credit institution or a notaire until the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce issues the certificate of incorporation or the capital-increase filing is registered. For transactions at or above EUR 750,000, the French receiving bank must report the flow to the Banque de France under the balance-of-payments survey within the statutory monthly deadline; there is no prior-approval requirement. Same-day EUR finality is achieved through TARGET2. Where a non-EU investor acquires control of the French manufacturing entity, an assessment under the French foreign-investment screening regime (CMF Article L151-3; Décret 2019-1590) must be performed; the manufacture of surgical endoscopes and laparoscopy towers generally does not fall within the protected sectors unless the activity includes R&D on critical technologies such as AI-driven surgical imaging or cybersecurity of connected devices, in which case a pre-closing authorization from the DG Trésor may be required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement rails ranked by operational preference: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments to EEA component suppliers, executed through STEP2/TARGET2 with one-business-day finality and no correspondent charges; (2) SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer for hard-currency payments to non-EEA suppliers, notably USD and CNY for Japanese CMOS sensors and German optical modules, with two-day value dating and full BPSS compliance; (3) SWIFT MT700 irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued by the French relationship bank for bulk procurement of 4K CMOS sensors, rigid endoscope lenses, and LED light-source modules where the supplier requires LC-at-sight or 60-day tenor, with confirmation added by the beneficiary's advising bank under ICC UCP 600; (4) documentary collections via MT400 series as a fallback for medium-risk suppliers with an established shipping record; (5) internal disbursement controls requiring dual-director signature authorization for any wire above EUR 10,000 and a 30-day payment calendar aligned with the LC tenor. USD disbursements must be sourced from the SAS natural USD position or from an FX hedge rather than spontaneous conversion to reduce transaction costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward FX contracts (change à terme) on EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, and EUR/JPY with a maturity of up to 24 months, documented under the French Banking Federation (FBF) master agreement and supported by a board-approved treasury policy; each hedge must be back-to-back with a commercial invoice, purchase order, or confirmed LC exposure.
FX swaps (swap de change) combining a spot transaction with a mirror forward leg, used for bridging temporary USD or CNY surpluses and deficits in the working-capital cycle, typically 3-6 months.
Cross-currency swaps (swap de devises) for long-dated exposures exceeding 12 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 or FBF master agreement with a credit support annex reflecting the SAS credit profile.
European-style purchased FX options (options de change) used solely as protection on EUR/USD conversion cost for large, known trade payables; writing of options is prohibited by treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible only for currencies without a deliverable onshore market (e.g., offshore CNH structural fallback) where the bank confirms that no deliverable forward market is reasonably available; NDFs are not permitted for EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, or other liquid convertible pairs, and every NDF use must be justified in writing to the bank's compliance desk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Comptes annuels (annual statutory accounts, comprising bilan, compte de résultat and annexe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court), filed through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve the accounts within 6 months of each financial year-end; the approved accounts must be deposited with the Registry within 2 months after approval, giving an effective maximum of 8 months from year-end if approval is taken at the end of the legal period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit triggers a formal injunction issued by the Registry or the Commercial Court under Article L.232-23 of the French Commercial Code, administrative fine up to €1,500 per legal representative under Article R.247-6, and persistent non-compliance may lead to compulsory strike-off (radiation) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO declaration) - annual exactness confirmation or change statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (RCS register) through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation is due simultaneously with the deposit of annual accounts; any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 15 days of the legal event giving rise to the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a complete and exact declaration is a criminal offence under Article L.561-47 of the Monetary and Financial Code: up to €30,000 fine and 6 months imprisonment for the legal representative, and €150,000 fine for the legal entity, plus registry blocking and disqualification from regulated activities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Liasse fiscale annuelle (annual corporate income tax return, Form 2065-SD and corresponding schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), French Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, return must be filed by the second business day following 1 May of the year after the closing period; for non-calendar financial years, return is due within 90 days of the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after formal notice incurs a penalty of 10% of the tax due; increasing to 40% if not filed within 30 days after formal notice and 80% in cases of fraudulent manoeuvres, plus monthly late interest of 0.2% and potential criminal sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) must be appointed if the French SAS exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at the financial year-end: total balance sheet exceeding €4,000,000; net turnover exceeding €8,000,000; average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Appointment is also mandatory when the SAS controls or is controlled by another entity, or when shareholders representing at least 10% of capital validly require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général / règlements ANC, as codified in the French Commercial Code); consolidated financial statements, if any, are prepared under IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under French law, the UBO declaration is filed at incorporation and updated within 15 days of any change in beneficiary-owner details. In addition, at each annual accounts deposit, the legal representative must confirm that the registered beneficial-owner information remains exact. Where no change has occurred, the annual accounts filing includes a confirmation statement without a separate substantive filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des mouvements de titres / registre des actions)
Register of Directors (registre des décisions et informations légales)
Minute Book (registre des délibérations / registre des processus)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax rate. A qualifying small company may benefit from a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to applicable ownership, turnover, and paid-in-capital conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The French research tax credit generally equals 30% of eligible research expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that threshold. Qualifying new businesses may access temporary exemptions or reductions under specific territorial or investment regimes. Patent and qualifying intellectual-property income may benefit from a separate 10% regime, subject to nexus and documentation requirements. Tax depreciation, investment incentives, and sector-specific credits may reduce the effective rate but do not alter the 25% headline rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, filed electronically through the French tax administration professional portal at impots.gouv.fr using the EDI-TDFC or EFI channel. The return is accompanied by the applicable tax package, principally Forms 2050-SD through 2059-G-SD. Form 2572-SD is used for the corporate income tax balance and credit settlement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate income tax instalments are generally paid quarterly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the annual return is generally due on the second working day after 1 May of the following year. For another year-end, filing is generally due within three months after the year-end. The corporate income tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end, or by the 15th day of the fifth month for a 31 December year-end. Quarterly instalments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, fiscal year dates, tax office, business activity, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SAS as the taxpayer. Provide the French registered office and SIREN. Identify the foreign parent separately and do not substitute the parent tax identification number for the French entity's SIREN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss determined from the accounting result after French tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income and expenses attributable to the French SAS and taxable under French law. Apply arm's-length pricing to dealings with foreign group entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Extra-accounting additions and deductions reconciling accounting profit to taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose non-deductible expenses, exempt income, participation exemptions, depreciation differences, provisions, interest limitation adjustments, and other permanent or temporary differences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use of tax losses carried forward and taxable income remaining after loss utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French annual loss-utilization cap, generally EUR 1 million plus 50% of current-year taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Do not assume that a foreign group loss is available to the French SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, reductions, foreign tax credits, and other amounts reducing corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits legally available to the French entity and retain supporting expenditure schedules, certificates, and foreign-tax evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross and net fixed assets, inventories, receivables, cash, and other assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report assets legally or economically attributable to the French SAS. Separately track imported equipment, intra-group receivables, and capitalized development costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital, reserves, retained earnings, provisions, borrowings, trade payables, and related-party liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify foreign-parent loans, guarantees, shareholder current accounts, and other controlled transactions consistently with the transfer-pricing records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases, external charges, payroll, taxes, depreciation, provisions, financial charges, and exceptional expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that management fees, royalties, interest, warranty charges, and procurement charges are supported by agreements, benefit evidence, and arm's-length analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales, services, operating subsidies, financial income, and exceptional income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separate French sales, exports, intra-group sales, and revenue from bundled medical-device services. Reconcile revenue to VAT, customs, statutory accounts, and intercompany ledgers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax treatment of disposals of fixed assets and other capital transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify gains and losses under French rules and retain acquisition cost, depreciation, disposal, and valuation evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of accounting and tax results and relevant retained amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the tax result to the statutory accounts and shareholder-approved financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Movements in provisions and depreciation differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support provisions with identifiable, probable, and sufficiently quantified risks. Medical-device warranties and product-liability provisions require specific evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses arising in the year and losses carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain year-by-year schedules and distinguish French tax losses from foreign or consolidated group losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax payable, instalments, credits, balance, and refund position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to the 2065 return, bank payment references, instalment notices, and approved tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and other specified tax-credit information where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide foreign tax certificates and treaty documentation. Do not claim a foreign tax credit exceeding the French tax attributable to the relevant income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Specified transactions with related parties, including certain charges, loans, and remuneration items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile disclosures to the intercompany agreement register, general ledger, transfer-pricing documentation, and financial statements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge on tax due, increasing to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and up to 80% in cases involving fraudulent manoeuvres or abusive concealment. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, calculated under the French Tax Code. Underpayments may also trigger tax reassessment, interest, documentation penalties, and criminal referral.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2257-SD, annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration, filed electronically through the professional tax portal. Forms 2258-SD and supporting transfer-pricing documentation may apply where the statutory thresholds and documentation requirements are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due within six months after the corporate income tax return deadline. The declaration must be consistent with the local file, master file, accounts, and intercompany contracts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: French entity identification, fiscal year, turnover, gross assets, and group information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the foreign ultimate parent, immediate parent, controlled entities, and relevant consolidated group information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts and categories of controlled transactions, including purchases, sales, services, financing, royalties, and guarantees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross and net amounts by transaction category and counterparty jurisdiction. Reconcile to the general ledger and statutory accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer-pricing method, tested party, comparables, and resulting pricing outcome.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the method supported by the functional analysis and retain evidence for medical-device manufacturing, distribution, R&D, warranty, and financing activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business restructurings, transfers of functions or risks, and transfers or use of intangible property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose changes to manufacturing rights, regulatory know-how, trademarks, technical files, software, and distribution rights.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual transfer-pricing declaration may trigger a penalty generally equal to 0.5% of the amount of transactions not documented, subject to statutory minimums and maximums, or 5% of reassessed profits or transferred income where applicable. The tax administration may also impose a 40% penalty for deliberate non-compliance and reassess taxable income.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% domestic withholding tax generally applies to dividends and similar distributions paid by a French company to a non-resident. The rate may be reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, subject to beneficial-ownership, minimum holding, holding-period, anti-abuse, and other conditions. French domestic participation-exemption rules generally do not themselves eliminate withholding tax on payments to a non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, review principal-purpose and anti-abuse conditions, and apply the reduced rate only when the statutory administrative procedure permits relief at source. Where relief at source is unavailable, withhold at the domestic rate and submit the relevant refund claim, generally using the applicable French treaty refund form and supporting dividend vouchers, ownership evidence, tax-residence certificate, payment records, and corporate resolutions. Maintain the file for audit and renew residence certificates as required.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and similar payments to non-residents are generally subject to a 25% French withholding tax under domestic law, subject to treaty reductions and the EU Interest and Royalties Directive where applicable. Ordinary interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax, but exceptions apply, including payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions and certain anti-abuse or instrument-specific rules. Treaty rates vary and must be confirmed under the recipient's residence-country treaty. The recipient must generally be the beneficial owner and the payment must satisfy arm's-length and anti-abuse requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer-pricing documentation, including local-file and master-file requirements, generally applies where the French entity or relevant group meets the EUR 400,000,000 statutory threshold based on turnover or gross assets, or where the entity belongs to a group meeting the applicable threshold. A separate annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration generally applies at the EUR 150,000,000 threshold or where the entity belongs to a group meeting that threshold. Currency: EUR.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods where the selected method is supported by a documented functional and comparability analysis
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a standalone regime titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless required under French transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership standards, anti-abuse provisions, the principal-purpose test in treaties, controlled-foreign-company rules, interest limitation rules, and the general abuse-of-law doctrine. The French SAS should maintain genuine French functions, personnel, premises, decision-making, assets, risks, regulatory capability, and commercial rationale proportionate to its manufacturing and medical-device activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of French sales, fabricated expenses, false invoices, omitted intercompany income, falsified accounting records, or intentional misstatement of taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, administrative penalties generally ranging from 40% to 80% of the evaded tax, and criminal tax-fraud sanctions. Natural persons may face imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000, increased in aggravated cases to up to seven years and EUR 3,000,000. Corporate fines may be multiplied under French criminal-law rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur personal criminal liability, tax-solidarity liability for fraudulent or repeated non-payment, civil claims, management bans, and asset seizure. Travel restrictions are not automatic and require a specific legal or judicial basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting manufacturing margin, royalties, financing returns, warranty costs, or procurement profit to a foreign group entity without functions, assets, risks, or arm's-length support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, interest, transfer-pricing documentation penalties, penalties for inadequate or missing documentation, and potential 40% or 80% tax penalties where conduct is deliberate or fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed where they knowingly approve fraudulent arrangements, obstruct an audit, or organize insolvency. Normal arm's-length adjustments generally remain liabilities of the SAS.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a French SAS as a nominal invoicing, royalty, financing, or distribution vehicle with no genuine personnel, premises, decision-making, manufacturing capability, or commercial risk assumption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, withholding-tax reassessment, transfer-pricing adjustment, abuse-of-law recharacterization, interest, and penalties. Transactions may be disregarded or reattributed to the entity performing the actual functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for breach of management duties and criminal liability where the structure is used to commit fraud. Corporate separateness is not normally disregarded solely because ownership is foreign.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through a conduit entity that lacks beneficial ownership, commercial purpose, or control over the relevant income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of reduced treaty or EU rates, application of domestic withholding tax, repayment of underwithheld tax, interest, and anti-abuse penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where they knowingly certify false residence, ownership, or beneficial-ownership facts. The SAS may remain jointly responsible for unpaid withholding tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or royalties without withholding, applying treaty relief without a valid residence certificate, or failing to report and remit withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax from the French payer, late-payment interest, and applicable filing or tax penalties. Treaty relief may be denied if procedural or substantive requirements are not met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal liability for deliberate non-remittance or fraudulent withholding arrangements and may be subject to criminal proceedings in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining false books, backdating contracts, recording fictitious suppliers, concealing related-party balances, or destroying audit evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties, rejection of accounts, criminal accounting offenses, confiscation, and potential imprisonment and fines under French criminal law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and accountants who participate in falsification may be prosecuted personally. Civil claims may include restitution and damages; management bans may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, sanctions, and suspicious payment activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unexplained third-party payments, opaque intermediaries, sanctioned counterparties, cash structuring, falsified end-user certificates, or transactions inconsistent with medical-device supply chains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transaction blocking, account restrictions, administrative sanctions, confiscation, criminal fines, and imprisonment depending on the offense. AML reporting failures may trigger professional and regulatory penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal criminal exposure for knowing participation, facilitation, concealment, or negligent governance. Travel bans may be imposed only by competent authorities under applicable proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Importing or selling laparoscopic towers without required conformity documentation, CE-marking compliance, registration, traceability, customs classification accuracy, or product-safety controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Product seizure, recalls, market withdrawal, customs reassessment, administrative fines, suspension of operations, and criminal sanctions for serious unsafe-product or customs offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal criminal or civil liability for knowingly placing non-compliant or unsafe devices on the market. Product-liability exposure may extend to bodily injury and consequential damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing to incur debts while insolvent, preferring related creditors, transferring assets offshore, stripping working capital, or paying dividends while unable to meet due debts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Insolvency proceedings, clawback of transactions, repayment orders, asset recovery, management bans, and possible criminal bankruptcy sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may order contribution to insufficient assets, impose personal bankruptcy restrictions, or prohibit management. Corporate veil piercing is exceptional but personal liability can arise from a director's management fault.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to preserve tax and transfer-pricing evidence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing intercompany agreements, unsupported management charges, absent comparables, inconsistent ledgers, incomplete customs records, or inability to produce records during a tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Documentation penalties, adverse inference, rejection of deductions, transfer-pricing reassessment, withholding-tax exposure, and applicable late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil or administrative liability for systematic governance failures and personal liability where non-preservation is intentional obstruction or part of a fraud.
